newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures end lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures end lower in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended mostly lower as the market started the week on a lackluster note, traders said.
"It was a totally meaningless day today," one Eurodollar futures floor trader said, referring to the bond and Eurodollar futures market's three-week ranges.
"You feel like you are working the night session except with a bigger crowd," a bond futures floor source said.
The rest of the week will be filled with a heavy schedule of U.S. economic reports and indicators -- some key, some minor -- that may give prices direction ahead of Friday.
Traders and analysts are focusing on the key U.S. labor statistics for October, which will be released on Friday.
Tuesday's U.S. third-quarter employment cost index could influence the market. The index, which will be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, is forecast to rise 0.8 percent, the same as the prior report.

Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, said bond and Eurodollar futures' coiling, consolidative price action over the last several sessions has duplicated the action last seen on September 24, the day the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) met.
"The technicals have been preluding a break-out," Grauer said.

He added that any break-out would be out of the symmetrical triangular pattern that has been forming for the last 10 sessions and will be completed on Friday -- the day the nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate will be released.

"All we can say is we can expect at least a one point move," he said, adding that opposing weekly and daily stochastics lower the chance for a move greater than one point. Daily stochastics point to a downtrend, while weekly stochastics indicate an uptrend.

He also noted that 60- and 100-minute stochastics have been vacillating wildly in the last five consecutive days. The stochastics have been reversing directions within a day, compared to normally swinging within three days for the 60-minute charts and five days for the 100-minute charts.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were down 03/32 110-29/32, 10-year notes were off 01/32 at 108-15/32, munibonds were off 11/32 at 114-00, March T-bills were steady at 904.82, March and June Eurodollars were down one basis point at 94.30 and 94.16, respectively. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
